entries.title: Elwynn Forest
body: A great woodland of stately hardwoods, rushing rivers and lakes, lying below the foothills of Blackrock Mountain. It is the heartland of the kingdom of Stormwind. The capital stands proudly in the north-western hills, and the forest's farms, lumber camps and mines have fed and supplied it for twelve centuries.

Its people are hardy and hard-working: loggers, farmers, fishers and miners, and breeders of the Evendale horses prized across the kingdom. Much of the forest burned during the First War, when the orcs swept through on their way to the capital, but the trees and glades have grown back, and today only a few broken orcish catapults, rotting in the grass, remember the occupation.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Elwynn Forest (History, People and culture, Geography)

entries.title: Northshire Valley
body: A pristine valley in the hills east of Stormwind, ringed by impassable mountains. Its only entrance, a pass to the south, is closed by thick stone walls and a guarded gate. A river runs through it and down into Crystal Lake.

The valley has not always been so peaceful. During the Second War, while the Horde held the ruins of the south, the abbey grounds served as the headquarters of Cho'gall's Twilight's Hammer clan. Today the Stormwind Guard keeps a garrison here under Marshal McBride, and the valley's vineyards were once the pride of the kingdom.

entries.title: Northshire Abbey
body: The seat of the Brotherhood of Northshire. Centuries ago, clerics of the young Church of the Holy Light came south from Lordaeron to spread their faith, founded the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, and built this abbey. Since then the clerics have comforted Stormwind's people in hard times and fought beside its armies. It was here that the young Guardian Medivh was cared for during the years he lay in a coma.

In the First War the clerics followed their abbot into battle, and the sacred Tome of Divinity, once stolen by ogres and recovered from the Deadmines, was kept here. The abbey was destroyed in the orcish onslaught, but refugees carried its holy books out of the rubble to Lordaeron. After the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild it.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Elwynn Forest (Great Wars and aftermath)

entries.title: Northshire Vineyards
body: The vineyards just east of the abbey, sheltered by the valley's walls. Their wine was the pride of Stormwind's cellars.
Lately the vineyards have been overrun by bandits of the Defias Brotherhood, who drove off the farmers and occupied the fields almost within sight of the abbey's guards.

entries.title: Goldshire
body: The largest town in Elwynn after the capital itself, at the crossroads of the roads to Stormwind, Northshire, Westfall and Redridge. Goldshire grew up soon after the kingdom's founding, as Stormwind's population spread into the forest. In the Gnoll War, seventy-five years before the Dark Portal opened, Redridge gnolls attacked it and were driven off by the Stormwind Army.

In the First War, Goldshire and Moonbrook were the last two towns to fall to the Horde, taken so that Warchief Blackhand could cut King Llane off from his people before the sack of the capital. After the Second War, the Alliance rebuilt it under Turalyon's supervision. Marshal Dughan of the Stormwind Guard keeps order there now.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Elwynn Forest (Founding of Stormwind, Great Wars)

entries.title: The Lion's Pride Inn
body: Goldshire's inn, one of the most respectable ale houses in Azeroth, whose motto is "Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold." The Farley family has run it since the days of King Llane Wrynn, and they take care to run an honest house.

It is perhaps the busiest inn outside any city. Travellers, soldiers and adventurers bound for every corner of the kingdom pass through its doors, and the green outside rarely goes a day without a duel.

entries.title: Fargodeep Mine
body: An old Stormwind gold mine south of Goldshire, with a lower gallery known simply as the Lower Mines. Its gold helped pay for the kingdom's wars.
It was abandoned, and a clan of kobolds has moved in. Kobolds are territorial and greedy, and they defend their candles and tunnels fiercely against anyone who comes looking for the gold.

entries.title: Jasperlode Mine
body: Like Fargodeep, Jasperlode was one of Elwynn's key mining sites, supplying Stormwind with the raw materials it needed for its wars. Kobolds have since overrun it, and with the army stretched thin, the kingdom has no soldiers to spare to drive them out.
The kobolds are not the mine's only tenants. A colony of mine spiders has taken its deepest tunnels and treats the kobolds as a ready meal, and their queen, Mother Fang, does not welcome visitors.

entries.title: The Stonefield and Maclure Farms
body: Two farmsteads in southern Elwynn, the Stonefield farm and the Maclure vineyards, whose families have been bitter rivals for as long as anyone remembers. The Maclures' vineyards and the Stonefields' fields lie close enough for every slight to be noticed.
Despite the feud, a son of one family and a daughter of the other have fallen in love, and some hope their love may yet bring the two families together.

entries.title: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch
body: A farmstead in south-eastern Elwynn, once the home of the Brackwell family, best known in the county for Princess, their huge prize-winning sow, who grew fat on the Stonefields' vegetables.
Bandits of the Defias Brotherhood have since taken the farm, and no one knows what became of the Brackwells.

entries.title: Tower of Azora
body: A small mage tower on the road between Goldshire and Eastvale, home of the Archmage Theocritus and his household of gnomish servants. Things that stray too near it tend to be changed by its magical aura; the servants have to fight off living buckets and mutant butterflies.
Azora's masters have long feuded with the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge, and each side spies on the other by magic. At the top of the tower, the Eye of Azora lets its keeper watch Ilgalar from afar.

entries.title: Eastvale Logging Camp
body: A string of lumber mills and homes in eastern Elwynn near the Redridge border, the centre of the forest's timber trade. Orders pour in from buyers across the kingdom, and the lumberjacks work to hard deadlines.

The noble house of Lord Joran Tremaind made its fortune in Eastvale lumber, and says it owes much to the people of Westfall. Marshal Haggard, once leader of the Stormwind Guard, retired to a manor here a few years ago.

entries.title: Stone Cairn Lake and Heroes' Vigil
body: A ring-shaped lake in north-eastern Elwynn around a large island. On the island stands Heroes' Vigil, a circle of stones around the Stone of Remembrance, a monument to those who died when the orcs sacked Goldshire and the lands around it in the First War. The lake takes its name from the cairn.
It was once a quiet place of pilgrimage. Now rogue wizards have settled on the island, and murlocs have raised their huts along the southern shore.

entries.title: Westbrook Garrison
body: A barracks of the Stormwind Guard at Forest's Edge, guarding Elwynn's western border with Westfall.

Its soldiers have had a hard time of it. With the bulk of the army abroad and the court troubled by Lady Katrana Prestor's influence, they barely have the men to keep the roads safe from the gnolls and thieves coming out of Westfall.

entries.title: Ridgepoint Tower
body: One of the Stormwind Guard's scout towers in Elwynn, standing over the south-eastern road. It watches for gnolls and orcs coming from Redridge, undead from Duskwood, and the Defias from their nearby camps.

entries.title: Mirror Lake
body: A small lake with a beautiful waterfall in western Elwynn, below the walls of the capital, beside an orchard and a cottage. The sewers of the Stormwind Stockade empty into it.

It would be an ideal spot for swimming and fishing, if Defias bandits had not taken over the orchard. The mages of the city's Wizard's Sanctum keep an eye on its waters too: the magical upheavals of recent years have altered the flow of magic around Stormwind, and they fear what it may do to those who drink here.

entries.title: Jerod's Landing
body: A boat landing on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti river, on the border with Duskwood. The Defias Brotherhood has taken it over, and its dockmaster and his men smuggle stolen goods from Redridge downriver to the Brotherhood's tower in Westfall.

entries.title: Marshal McBride
body: Marshal Douglas McBride of the Stormwind Guard commands the garrison of Northshire Abbey and the defence of the valley. The abbey serves as a recruiting and training ground for anyone brave enough to help keep the kingdom's peace, and McBride is the first officer many of them meet.

entries.title: Marshal Dughan
body: The officer of the Stormwind Army in charge of Goldshire and the lands around it. He worries about the kobolds to the north and the gnolls and thieves to the west, and wants to know how far they have spread.
Dughan is a practical man who keeps the peace with few soldiers, and has the habit of seeing the town's young troublemakers as future inmates of the Stockade.

entries.title: Hogger
body: The chieftain of the Riverpaw gnolls, a huge gnoll who has overpowered every attempt to capture him. In the years after the Third War, his pack became an ominous threat to the kingdom, raiding farms and villages throughout Elwynn.

The Riverpaws are not acting alone. The Defias Brotherhood supplies them with weapons, tactics and magic. The Stormwind Army has placed a generous bounty on Hogger's head, and wanted posters for him hang on every guard post on the western road.

entries.title: Archmage Theocritus
body: An eccentric archmage who once belonged to the Kirin Tor of Dalaran, and left to live independently in the Tower of Azora. He keeps a coterie of attendants, from legions of gnomish servants to his own personal clothier.

Theocritus takes little interest in the daily affairs of the kingdom, but considers it his duty to oppose the fallen mage Morganth of Redridge, both as a personal enemy and as a threat to Stormwind. He has spent months learning to listen through the pendants Morganth's gnolls wear.

entries.title: The Founding of Stormwind
body: About twelve hundred years before the Dark Portal opened, descendants of the Arathi bloodline, led by Faldir, left the empire of Arathor in the north and travelled south past the mountains of Khaz Modan. After many long seasons they settled in a fertile valley, in the land they named Azeroth, and founded the kingdom of Stormwind.

The kingdom quickly became a power in its own right. Its farmsteads prospered, its people multiplied, and towns like Goldshire grew up in the forest around the capital. Clerics came from Lordaeron and built Northshire Abbey, and the realm stood largely untroubled until the orcs came through the Dark Portal.

entries.title: The First War in Elwynn
body: When the orcish Horde came, Brightwood, Westfall and Redridge fell first. Thousands of orcs marched through Elwynn and surrounded the capital, cutting it off from everything but the sea. When the Bleeding Hollow and Twilight's Hammer clans assaulted the walls, Anduin Lothar led the Knights of Stormwind through the forest and fell on their rear, and the orcs fled.

A year later they returned. Goldshire and Moonbrook fell, Stormwind Keep was sacked, and King Llane was dead. Lothar, now regent, led the survivors north to Lordaeron aboard thousands of boats, and the Stormreaver clan lorded over the ruins. The Stone of Remembrance at Heroes' Vigil honours the dead of those years.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Elwynn Forest (Great Wars and aftermath)

entries.title: The Stonemasons' Debt
body: After the Second War, rebuilding Stormwind became the kingdom's first task, and Turalyon oversaw the return of its people to Elwynn. The Stonemasons' Guild under Edwin VanCleef spent years raising the capital again from its ruins.

When the time came to pay them, the House of Nobles could not: it had run up a huge debt expanding the army through Elwynn and into Stranglethorn. When VanCleef demanded restitution, the nobles ordered the guild disbanded. Riots followed, in which Queen Tiffin Wrynn was killed, and the masons who fled the city became the Defias Brotherhood.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Elwynn Forest (Great Wars and aftermath)
